sources.entry: mise - A polyglot tool version manager that installs Python versions and reads .python-version files.

summary.one_liner: mise (mise-en-place) is a polyglot CLI that manages a project's dev tool versions, environment variables, and tasks from a single mise.toml file.
summary.what_it_does: It installs dev tools such as Node.js, Python, Go, Rust, and Terraform at per-project versions, drawing from a registry of 1,000+ tools or directly from backends like GitHub releases, Aqua, Cargo, npm, and PyPI. It loads environment variables, .env files, PATH entries, virtualenvs, and secrets automatically when you enter a directory. It runs tasks defined in mise.toml or in mise-tasks/ scripts, with dependencies, parallel execution, and file watching. It also reads existing version files such as .tool-versions, .nvmrc, and .python-version once enabled. Finally, mise bootstrap and mise dot apply can set up a machine with system packages, dotfiles, Git repositories, macOS defaults, and background services.
use_cases: manage per-project Python and Node.js versions
load .env files and environment variables per directory
bootstrap a new machine with packages and dotfiles
pin exact tool versions with a lockfile
stack: Shell integration (bash, zsh, fish, PowerShell, Nushell, Elvish, Xonsh)
notable: Single mise.toml covers tools, env vars, and tasks together
Installs tools from multiple backends including GitHub releases, Aqua, Cargo, npm, and PyPI
mise bootstrap and dotfile commands configure whole machines, not just projects
mise lock writes exact versions and checksums to mise.lock
caveats: Machine bootstrap, dotfile, and service features are a larger scope to adopt than basic version management; the README suggests adopting only the parts you need
Shell activation is optional but needed for automatic PATH and environment updates on directory change
README does not state platform limits beyond install instructions for macOS, Linux, and Windows
